It does not discuss prices or price moves, is not investment advice, and does not recommend any token, platform or stock.

chapters.intro: Monologue: AI add-on packs and used jet engines
chapters.mc-scene: Main Course: Can one phone call keep AI in check?
chapters.fm-intro: Follow the Money: Moving the stock ledger onto a blockchain

d002.text: This is Tech Signal, where we pick today's real signal out of all the noise.

hk01.text: Today's main course: Trump talked AI safety on the US TV news show 60 Minutes.

hk02.text: He said the government told an AI boss: "Get ready to go to jail."

q001.text: If an AI firm messes up and the government calls its boss about jail, is that protection or scaring off innovation?

q002.text: We'll fight it out in the main course.

q003.text: First, two more stories from yesterday, November 9.

a001.text: First, per The Verge, Apple's music app Logic Pro now sells extra AI usage.

a002.text: So some Apple AI features have caps, and when you run out, you can pay for more.

a004.text: Fine by me. At least I choose whether to buy more.

a005.text: Apple calls it the Intelligence Usage Pack: one purchase, $49.99.

a006.text: Leftovers roll over monthly, but expire 12 months after purchase.

a007.text: The caps exist because some features run on OpenAI or Google Gemini cloud models.

a008.text: Cloud models are AI on remote servers.

a009.text: And the pack works only for the buyer's Apple account. No Family Sharing.

a010.text: Families share everything, but not this AI?

a011.text: Apple says the cap depends on how complex your chats with Logic Pro's AI assistant are.

a012.text: Like phone data: the more complex the chat, the faster it drains.

a015.text: Here's my every-episode question: should I get a new phone?

a016.text: No. This time you're paying for AI, not a phone.

j001.text: Second, per Decrypt, AI data center builders are hunting used turbines, even retired jet engines.

j002.text: Data centers need power, and new power gear takes too long.

j003.text: A gas turbine burns natural gas to spin a generator.

j006.text: Decrypt cites an energy consultancy: new US gas turbines take six years on average to arrive.

j007.text: Like ordering in first grade and getting it as you finish sixth.

j008.text: By then, the chips inside will be obsolete!

j009.text: One fix: turn jet engine tech into power generators.

j010.text: Smart. Retired plane engines get new jobs.

j011.text: Decrypt says used turbines are cheaper and may come sooner.

j012.text: But supply is thin, upkeep is hard, and pollution permits are needed.

j015.text: My old question: should I get a new phone?

j016.text: No. Even data centers are buying used.

t001.text: Third, our main course: per The Verge, Trump talked AI safety in a US TV interview.

t002.text: So, is a jail warning protection or a scare? Let's argue.

m001.text: Picture this: a big AI company's boss gets a call from the government.

m002.text: Trump himself described that call on the show.

m003.text: Trump said someone was reported for doing something bad with AI, and the government called them very strongly.

m004.text: He said they were told: "Get ready to go to jail. Please give your wife a kiss good night."

m005.text: Wait, isn't there a formal process? One call and done?

m007.text: The show asked him about AI executives' warnings on their own models' safety.

m008.text: AI safety here means the risk of AI being misused, or failing and hurting people.

m009.text: He said the risk is "not nearly as real" as executives say, and it "can be managed, and it's managed."

m010.text: Per The Verge's report, he meant the US Justice Department manages that risk.

m011.text: The Justice Department prosecutes federal crimes.

m012.text: So the risk isn't that real, yet his example is a jail warning.

m013.text: For AI firms, the scary part is not knowing if the risk is big or small.

m014.text: So who? Trump wouldn't name the person or the company.

m015.text: He only said an AI company leader, "one of the big ones."

m016.text: He said after the arrest threat, "this person totally changed everything."

m017.text: It worked? More like scared stiff.

m018.text: What changed? He didn't say. Nor did the report.

m019.text: To be clear, this is Trump's own account, via The Verge.

m020.text: No second source, and no reply from the Justice Department or the company.

m021.text: I pick the industry. AI must move fast to build good things.

m022.text: If one call can threaten a boss with jail, who'll dare build AI?

m023.text: I'm on the other side. Someone must hold AI firms accountable.

m024.text: But a threat isn't a rule.

m029.text: Rules that detailed? By the time you finish, others are way ahead.

m030.text: On this, Trump sounded like you on the show. Guess what he said?

m031.text: He said, "I don't mind guardrails, but I don't want to put us in a deep second position."

m032.text: Guardrails are AI safety rules and limits. I want some, just not so many we stall.

m033.text: You want guardrails, ideally in someone else's lane.

m034.text: He said he "absolutely would" work with Democrats on AI safety.

m035.text: But which guardrails, and when? The report never says.

m036.text: Like getting a failing grade before the syllabus is out.

m037.text: No founder would sign up for that class.

m043.text: The report doesn't mention Taiwan; in Asia, only China.

m069.text: That's Trump's claim: China has no guardrails, theirs are "whatever President Xi says goes."

m047.text: For firms, clear penalties matter most. Any fine is easier to predict than a call, right?

m051.text: So per the report, it's a phone call, not written rules.

m052.text: And firms don't know who gets the next call. That's scariest.

m053.text: AI builders lose. Bosses never know when the call comes.

m054.text: Ordinary people lose too: we can't see or check what changed.

m055.text: Big firms have lawyers. More rules, and small ones fall first, right?

m056.text: Agreed. Complex rules hit small companies first.

m058.text: One: will the Justice Department or the company confirm the call?

m060.text: Two: will his guardrail talks with Democrats become written rules?

m061.text: Three: how is the risk he calls "managed" managed?

m062.text: Did the call happen, and to whom? I don't know. It's only his word.

m063.text: Still with industry: let it run, and use the law if it breaks.

m064.text: Jail threats just drive builders away first.

m065.text: My view: AI firms must be accountable, and Kai's worry about scaring off innovation is real.

m066.text: But accountability without fear needs written rules everyone can see, not a phone call.

f002.text: Per Decrypt, NYSE parent ICE plans a platform to trade stocks recorded on a blockchain.

f042.text: Ava Labs, Avalanche's developer, says this platform's books will be kept on Avalanche.

f045.text: A legacy exchange plus blockchain? Two worlds, I thought.

f043.text: After a trade, cash and shares must still swap. That's clearing and settlement.

f003.text: The blockchain goes into exactly that step. Decrypt calls it the market's plumbing.

f004.text: I thought a trade ended there. What's left?

f006.text: One, the trade: both sides agree.

f007.text: Two, clearing: who owes what to whom.

f008.text: Three, settlement: shares and money swap, and it's done.

f009.text: Online shopping: checkout is the trade, the store's tally is clearing, paid and delivered is settlement.

f010.text: So Avalanche does the tally and handover?

f011.text: Right. The clearing firm doing that will use Avalanche as its core ledger.

f013.text: A ledger records every trade and who owns what.

f041.text: Blockchain I know: a ledger many computers share, hard to change once written.

f014.text: Tokenization means issuing assets like stocks and funds as blockchain tokens.

f015.text: So the stock's the same; only the record keeper changes.

f017.text: The goal: 24/7 trading, clearing and settlement, pending regulatory approval.

f019.text: Without regulators' OK, it has no first day yet.

f020.text: NYSE's digital issuance chief said the exchange picks the right tech for each job.

f049.text: He said it will support stocks on several blockchains.

f021.text: But the ledger that records and settles trades has conditions. Guess?

f039.text: Practical. Stocks on many chains, one rock-solid ledger.

f026.text: Decrypt calls it a sign Wall Street's old guard is moving core systems onto public blockchains.

f047.text: Public chains are usually open to all, but the NYSE executive says this ledger controls who joins.

f040.text: Putting it under trading beats wrapping one stock in a token.

f050.text: Rare: no new-phone question this time.

f027.text: Who pays whom, and how much? The report doesn't say.

f025.text: So we follow the pipes, not the money.

f029.text: One: ICE also plans a tokenized stock platform with crypto exchange OKX.

f036.text: The Magnificent Seven are seven big US tech stocks, including Apple and Meta.

f048.text: All seven opted out of tokenization on the ICE and OKX platform.

f031.text: Apple shows up twice: selling AI packs, and refusing tokenization.

f030.text: Two: an IMF study found real demand for tokenized stocks, but they're hard to trade.

f032.text: Also, Decrypt warns the pipes may be built before demand catches up.

f033.text: Like a subway station built before the riders.

f034.text: Build first, I say. Wait for riders and you're late.

f035.text: Note: this covers only the pipes. It's not investment advice, and we recommend no token or platform.

s001.text: Honestly, today's key story is Trump on AI safety.

s002.text: My big unknown: what guardrails he'd agree with Democrats. The report says nothing.

s003.text: Our tip: before buying an AI add-on pack, check family sharing and expiry.

s004.text: Most patient today: data centers awaiting turbines ordered in first grade, due by sixth.

s005.text: By then, everyone will know my question by heart.
